rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding titles of might and wisdom are demonstrated by the precision and firmness of God's acts in creating the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: دل عليها باتقان أفعاله وإحكامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads ترونها either as modifying the pillars or as a separate clause: invisible supports would show subtle wisdom, while unsupported heavens display sheer power.
rows.anchor: إن قلنا إنه صفة لعمد أو استئناف

words: وَأَلْقَىٰ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set mountains in the earth to keep it from swaying beneath people; the verse marvelously speaks of mountains as cast onto it although familiar mountains are below.
rows.anchor: الرواسي التي تعرفونها تكون من تحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After making the earth stable for settlement, God dispersed every kind of animal across it.
rows.anchor: فقال منبها لمظهر العظمة على أن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone sends rain from heaven, an act no creature can bring about, and rain then supplies the means of nourishment.
rows.anchor: ما لا قدرة لمخلوق عليه بوجه

words: فَأَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A كريم زوج is a plant kind, alike in type and beautiful, fresh, pleasing, useful, and abundant enough to sustain the animals.
rows.anchor: البهجة والنضرة الجالبة للسرور والمنفعة والكثرة الحافظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ordered creation establishes His might and wisdom, and therefore His sole divinity and the obligation to worship Him alone, just as He alone creates.
rows.anchor: وجوب توحيده في العبادة كما توحد بالخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything people observe is God's creation; He possesses unmatched majesty and has no equal.
rows.anchor: له جميع العظمة فلا كفوء له

words: فَأَرُونِى مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to show what the idols created rebukes their worship: no rational being should submit to an object that has performed no act warranting submission.
rows.anchor: فسأله في رؤية ما خلقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than merely answer that idols create nothing, God calls their worshippers entrenched wrongdoers, placing things wrongly under desire and living in manifest error.
rows.anchor: بل عبدتهم أو أنتم في جعلهم شركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining that some are kept from wisdom while others receive it, the discourse turns to Luqman as an earlier example of one who believed and placed things rightly.
rows.anchor: توقع السامع الإخبار عن بعض من آتاه الحكمة من المتقدمين الذين كانوا من المحسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai calls Luqman God's servant and defines wisdom as knowledge supported by action and action made sound through knowledge.
rows.anchor: العلم المؤيد بالعمل والعمل المحكم بالعلم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines wisdom as knowing the reason a judgment is required; judgment entails patience and perseverance, and wisdom grows with breadth of knowledge.
rows.anchor: الأمر الذي لأجله وجب الحكم

rows.speaker: ابن ميلق
rows.claim: Ibn Milq says wisdom consists in reaching truth and correctness in speech and action.
rows.anchor: مدارها على إصابة الحق والصواب في القول والعمل

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says a person is wise only when wisdom appears in both speech and conduct; merely speaking wisely is insufficient without practice.
rows.anchor: لا يقال لشخص حكيما حتى تجتمع له الحكمة في القول والفعل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying Luqman was not a prophet but a reflective, certain servant; after weighing the ordeal of judgeship, he accepted God's command and was granted wisdom.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما ان النبي ( ص ) قال : ( حقا أقول ! لم يكن لقمان نبيا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet's saying that nine parts of wisdom lie in solitude and one in silence.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله قال

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqman says health is wealth and a good disposition is the greatest bliss.
rows.anchor: وقال لقمان : لا مال كصحة ولا نعيم كطيب نفس

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqman compares a father's correction of his child to rain from the sky that nourishes a crop.
rows.anchor: وقال لقمان : لا مال كصحة ولا نعيم كطيب نفس , وقال : ضرب الوالد لولده كالسماء للزرع

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Asked who is worst, Luqman answers: the person who does not care if others see him doing wrong.
rows.anchor: وقيل له : أي الناس شر ؟ قال : الذي لا يبالي أن يراه الناس مسيئا

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: When told his face was ugly, Luqman replies that the critic is faulting the design or its designer.
rows.anchor: وقيل له : ما أقبح وجهك ! فقال : تعيب النقش أو النقاش

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits Luqman's explanation of his attainment: truthful speech, fulfilling trusts, and leaving aside what does not concern him.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي : إنه قيل له : لم بلغت ما بلغت ؟ قال : بصدق الحديث وأداء الأمانة وترك ما لا يعنيني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wisely raises whomever He wills for sound nature, even a servant; likewise He chose Muhammad for prophethood and noble character despite his not being among worldly magnates.
rows.anchor: فهو سبحانه من حكمته وحكمه أن يرفع ما يشاء بما يعلمه منه سلامة الطبع وإن كان عبدا

rows.speaker: ابن ميلق
rows.claim: Ibn Milq says God's wisdom alternates justice and grace, appearing as abasement or elevation, poverty or wealth, sickness or healing, and death or continued life.
rows.anchor: من حكمته سبحانه أن يجمع بين أثرى عدله وفضله

rows.speaker: ابن ميلق
rows.claim: Ibn Milq says effects of justice and favor may be inward, outward, split between inward and outward, or alternate; the later effect corresponds to the earlier one.
rows.anchor: غير أن أثر العدل والفضل فد يتعلق بالبواطن خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God applies justice outwardly to His chosen servants, then follows it with favor inwardly and outwardly, completing their education and refinement through trial.
rows.anchor: أجرى الله سبحانه آثارعدله على ظواهر أصفيائه دون بواطنهم

rows.speaker: ابن ميلق
rows.claim: Ibn Milq says divine wisdom can place earthly rule in the hands of the formerly vulnerable, citing the Negus, sold in childhood; the recurring trials of great people from Adam onward illustrate this pattern.
rows.anchor: للمستضعفين فيها كالنجاشي حيث بيع في صغره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes أن اشكر as an implied command from God, which amounts to granting Luqman gratitude; naming God explicitly emphasizes His unique majesty in this context of wisdom.
rows.anchor: يؤول إلى ( آتيناه الشكر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, أن is a masdariyya: Luqman was given wisdom because of gratitude.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون ( أن ) مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative form shows that Luqman's gratitude answered God's command, making it a higher form of gratitude.
rows.anchor: وعبر بفعل الأمر إعلاما بأن شكره كان لامتثال الأمر ليكون أعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense generalizes the promise: whoever turns to God in gratitude at any time benefits himself and continually receives God's increase while the deed endures.
rows.anchor: ويكون معروفه له دائما بدوام العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense suggests that even one occurrence of disbelief earns God's turning away, while disbelief harms only its perpetrator.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالماضي إشارة إلى أن من وقع منه كفر ولو مرة جوزي بالإعراض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, God needs no gratitude and is worthy of every praise even if all creation disbelieves; their inability to escape His decree itself manifests His might.
rows.anchor: له جميع المحامد وإن كفره جميع الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the nearer reading assigns غني to the disbeliever and حميد to the grateful; each person's choice affects only that person, while God is independent of the disbeliever's thanks and praised by the grateful.
rows.anchor: أن يعود ( غني ) إلى الكافر و ( حميد ) إلى الشاكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, the verse uses ellipsis: attributing gratitude's benefit to the self implies the omitted harm of disbelief, while the two divine attributes imply their omitted parallel in the earlier clause.
rows.anchor: تخصيص الشكر بالنفس أولا يدل على حذف مثله من الكفر ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes the wise person as continually recalling God's attributes of majesty and beauty, so fear outweighs hope in this troubled worldly abode.
rows.anchor: والحكيم من أدام استحضار صفات الجلال والجمال فغلب خوفه رجاءه ما دام في دار الأكدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives the wicked only brief enjoyment; believers should not rush to their punishment because every coming event is near, though the delay may look long to people.
rows.anchor: فإن كل آت قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نضطرهم means God seizes the arrogant so completely that they cannot escape by any stratagem; ثم also suggests the drawn-out humiliation of being driven to punishment.
rows.anchor: أي نأخذهم أخذا لا يقدرون على الانفكاك عنه بنوع حيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is severe, heavy, unending, and inescapable from every direction, like an enormous heavy mass pressing down on its victim.
rows.anchor: شديد ثقيل , لا ينقطع عنهم أصلا ولا يجدون لهم منه مخلصا

words: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers argue while admitting that God created heaven and earth, an admission that entails His exclusive creative lordship and should compel submission to His unity.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من أعجب العجب مجادلتهم مع إقرارهم بما يلزمهم به قطعا التسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For this surah's wisdom-oriented purpose it suffices to state the subject, الله; al-Zukhruf, whose aim is fuller exposition, uses a fuller formulation.
rows.anchor: لم يزد هنا على المسند إليه بخلاف الزخرف التي مبناها الإبانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confession shows that everything they associate with God is itself one of His created artifacts, not a partner in creation.
rows.anchor: فقد أقروا بأن كل ما أشركوا به بعض خلقه ومصنوع من مصنوعاته

rows.speaker: امرأة ذي النور الدرسي
rows.claim: A woman associated with Dhu al-Nur al-Dawsi asks whether children should be feared from the idol Dhu al-Shara, illustrating belief that idols could act.
rows.anchor: قالت امرأة ذي النور الدرسي رضي الله عنه : هل يخشى على الصبية من ذي الشرى

rows.speaker: قوم ضمام بن ثعلبة
rows.claim: When Dammam ibn Thaʿlaba's people heard him revile their gods, they warned him to beware leprosy and vitiligo, showing their fear of idols' power.
rows.anchor: وكما قال قوم ضمام بن ثعلبة رضي الله عنه لما سبب آلهتهم : اتق الجدام اتق البرص

rows.speaker: ثقيف
rows.claim: The custodian of al-ʿUwwa and Thaqif feared divine retaliation when their cult objects were attacked; after Thaqif said the foundations would rage, al-Mughira ibn Shuʿba excavated them.
rows.anchor: قالت ثقيف في طاغيتهم , حتى أنهم قالوا عندما سويت بالأرض , والله ليغضبن الأساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When afflicted, especially at sea, the idolaters disavow their idols and attribute events to God, as exclusive divine control requires.
rows.anchor: إذا مستهم الضراء لا سيما في البحر تبرؤوا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that most know God is the sole controller but fail to act on that knowledge; knowledge without practice is effectively no knowledge and may be worse than ignorance.
rows.anchor: إن الله هو المنفرد بكل شيء كما أنه تفرد بخلق السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they have no useful knowledge at all, since any knowledge of God would benefit them.
rows.anchor: أو يكون المعنى أنه لا علم لهم أصلا إذ لو كان لهم علم لنفعهم في علمهم بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that they do not affirm God's exclusive creation and provision, a contradiction that obliges them to accept the Prophet's claim of absolute divine unity.
rows.anchor: فيكون ذلك موجبا لتناقضهم وملزما لهم بالإقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in heaven and earth belongs exclusively to God because He made it; the disbelievers' own admission that He created it leaves no room for a partner.
rows.anchor: الملك الأعظم المحيط بجميع أوصاف الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding admission of creation, the verse need not repeat ما في and the preposition before الأرض; the prior proof already establishes its inclusion.
rows.anchor: لم يؤكد بإعادة { ما } والجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit divine name and emphatic هو answer the implied denial of God's self-sufficiency in associating partners with Him, and affirm these attributes without limitation.
rows.anchor: وأكد لأن ادعائهم الشريك يتضمن إنكار غناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is absolutely self-sufficient: all things belong to Him and depend on Him, while He needs nothing.
rows.anchor: ليس محتاجا إلى شيء أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves every praise as the absolute benefactor; every tongue praises Him, and even blameful speech is praise insofar as He caused it.
rows.anchor: المستحق لجميع المحامد , لأنه المنعم

words: وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَٰمٌ وَٱلْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if every earthly tree became a pen and the sea, supplied by seven further seas, became ink, God's words would not be exhausted before the pens and ink ran out.
rows.anchor: فكتب بتلك الأقلام وذلك المداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular شجرة is distributive and exhaustive: each tree in the earth is imagined as a pen.
rows.anchor: ودل على الاستغراق وتقصى كل فرد فرد من الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran reading puts البحر in the accusative, construed as ولو أن البحر, while the nominative reading makes it a new clause with the sea supplying more ink.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة البصريين بالنصب التقدير : ولو أن البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's words are inexhaustible; creative acts follow those words, so every word brings a matter into being, as the verse about His command to say كن explains.
rows.anchor: فلا تكون كلمة إلا الأحداث شأن من الشؤون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inability to exhaust even the few words explicitly mentioned proves a fortiori that the whole of God's words cannot be exhausted.
rows.anchor: بالعجز عن ذلك القليل فيفهم العجز عن الكلم من باب الأولى

words: أَقْلَٰمٌ وَٱلْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis: mentioning pens implies their omitted ink, and the seven seas imply seven trees in the imagined supply of pens.
rows.anchor: ذكر الأقلام دليلا على حذف مدادها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seven seas is hyperbole for great abundance, and أبحر uses a small plural for many; by contrast, كلمات retains the small plural's literal sense to make the incapacity to count even a little striking.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالسبعة المبالغة في الكثرة لا حقيقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is irresistible and His decisions cannot be undone; no creature has knowledge or wisdom beyond what He grants, and these attributes answer denial of His power and resurrection wisdom.
rows.anchor: ولا حكمة لأحد منهم إلا بمقدار ما اورثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because deniers think resurrection impossible after body parts mingle with earth, God points to their acknowledged example of souls being taken from bodies mixed among the earth's parts.
rows.anchor: وكان إنكارهم إنما هو بسبب اختلاط الأجزاء بالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Angel of Death takes each soul completely from its body after the body has mingled with soil throughout the lands, though people cannot distinguish its parts by ordinary means.
rows.anchor: بعد أن كانت مختلطة بجميع أجزاء البلدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive وكّل leaves the agent unstated to emphasize the ease and divine power behind the task; the creator commissioned the Angel of Death, His servant, to carry it out.
rows.anchor: ببناء الفعل لما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The body remains complete when the soul is removed, and soul-body mingling is closer than the body's mixing with soil; if a commissioned servant can do this, the Lord can distinguish every particle for resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإذا البدن ملقى لا روح في شيء منه وهو على حاله كاملا لا نقص في شيء منه يدعي الخلل بسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspoken next step is that God recreates them as they were at first; this resurrection is omitted because the context makes it clear.
rows.anchor: فحذفه كما هو عادة القرآن في حذف كل ما دل عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They return to the Lord who first created and nurtured them, are raised together before Him, and receive recompense; like a king with servants, He does not leave wrongdoers unattended.
rows.anchor: بأن يجازي كلا بما فعل , كما هو دأب الملوك مع عبيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from addressing the criminals to addressing the Prophet consoles him and signals contempt for them; the address may also be to anyone capable of seeing.
rows.anchor: عن خطابهم استهانة بهم وإيذانا بالغضب

words: وَلَوْ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُوا۟ رُءُوسَهُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb follows a particle normally associated with the past because the scene is certain, as though it already happened; this form lets listeners anticipate seeing the criminals' fate.
rows.anchor: لأنه لتحقق وقوعه كأن قد كان
